prompt.context_jp: だが、彼らを阻んだのは患者の傷ではなく、就労ビザという一枚の紙であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: だが、彼らを阻んだの___患者の傷ではなく、就労ビザという一枚の紙であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the cleft/identifying structure.

feedback.correct_en: This is a cleft construction (~のは…だ) that frames 'what blocked them' as the topic, then identifies it. The topic marker は is required here.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn it into a plain new-information subject and break the ~のは…ではなく…であった identification pattern. を doesn't fit the nominalized subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 私が買ったのは本です。
contrast_examples.en: What I bought is a book.

prompt.context_jp: 警視庁外事課の月島は、官邸からの返答をひたすら待ちながら、灰皿の縁を指で叩いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 警視庁外事課の月島___、官邸からの返答をひたすら待ちながら、灰皿の縁を指で叩いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the scene-setting topic of this sentence?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is shifting to Tsukishima as the established topic of this new scene and describing what he's doing. は sets him up as the theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal brand-new 'it is Tsukishima who…' identification, which doesn't match the scene-shift narration. に is a locative/goal marker and doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: It was Tsukishima who was waiting.

prompt.context_jp: 時計の針は、地下に取り残された人々の残り時間そのものを刻んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時計の針___、地下に取り残された人々の残り時間そのものを刻んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that sets 'the clock's hand' as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is making a thematic statement about the clock hands as a symbol — は presents it as topic and allows the broader metaphorical comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reduce it to a plain new-information report of motion and lose the thematic, symbolic framing the narration needs.

contrast_examples.en: The hands of the clock mark time (as topic/symbol).

prompt.context_jp: 彼が最初に口にしたのは、自分の痛みではなく肉親の名だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼が最初に口にしたの___、自分の痛みではなく肉親の名だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the cleft 'what he first said was…'.

feedback.correct_en: The ~のは…ではなく…だった cleft contrasts two possibilities. は marks the nominalized topic and sets up the contrastive identification.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as 'the thing he first said happened/existed,' breaking the identification + contrast reading the sentence needs.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が言ったのは名前だ。
contrast_examples.en: What he said was a name.

prompt.context_jp: 取調室の扉が音もなく開き、刑事が緊張した面持ちで一枚のメモを差し出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 取調室の扉___音もなく開き、刑事が緊張した面持ちで一枚のメモを差し出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for this fresh, visual event.

feedback.correct_en: This narrates a brand-new on-screen event — the door silently opening. が introduces the subject as new information in the described scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'the door' a topic we're commenting on, which clashes with the sudden, perceptual nature of the action.

prompt.context_jp: 「まともな政治家もいるようですね」
prompt.prompt_jp: まともな政治家___いるようですね。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle Otowa uses to acknowledge the existence of decent politicians.

feedback.correct_en: も signals 'even/also decent politicians exist' — acknowledging an added instance to the previously discussed indecisive ones. This is what the original line uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would narrow the comment to 'as for decent politicians…' which lacks the 'in addition' nuance. が would be plain existence without the contrast with the earlier indecisive politicians.

contrast_examples.en: There are also decent people (unexpected addition).

prompt.context_jp: 「この国で テロは起きない テロなど この国には存在しない」
prompt.prompt_jp: この国でテロ___起きない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Tsukishima's categorical denial.

feedback.correct_en: Tsukishima is making a sweeping topic-level claim about terrorism as a category: 'as for terror — it doesn't happen here.' は fits categorical negation.
feedback.incorrect_en: テロが起きない would describe a single non-occurrence in context, not the sweeping policy-stance generalization he's making.

contrast_examples.jp: ここで事故は起きない。

prompt.context_jp: 「どんな命も救う それがＭＥＲの存在意義です」
prompt.prompt_jp: どんな命___救う。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the correct particle for the direct object.

feedback.correct_en: どんな命も = 'any/every life' — the universal 'も' replaces the direct-object を to emphasize 'without exception.' This is Kitami's defining credo.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn 命 into the subject (lives save…?). は would narrow to 'as for any life,' losing the emphatic universal quantifier reading.

prompt.context_jp: 残り時間の掲示だけが、赤い数字で全員を追い立てていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 残り時間の掲示だけ___、赤い数字で全員を追い立てていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 'only the countdown display.'

feedback.correct_en: だけが gives exhaustive 'only X and nothing else' — among all the chaos, that one thing is what's driving everyone. The exhaustive-listing が is required with だけ here.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would shift to 'at least X' / contrastive 'as for only that,' losing the exhaustive 'nothing but' urgency.

contrast_examples.en: You alone are what I can rely on.

prompt.context_jp: 重い扉の向こうにいる十五の命が、彼らの背中を押していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 重い扉の向こうにいる十五の命___、彼らの背中を押していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this freshly introduced subject.

feedback.correct_en: The 'fifteen lives' are newly described with a relative clause and introduced into the scene as the force pushing them forward. が marks this new-information subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require those fifteen lives to be already established as topic; here the whole noun phrase is being presented fresh.

contrast_examples.jp: 向こうにいる人が助けを待っている。
contrast_examples.en: The people on the other side are waiting for help (new intro).

contrast_examples.jp: あの人は助けを待っている。
contrast_examples.en: That person is waiting for help (known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 「地下に閉じ込められた人間は 不法労働者だ そんな連中のために 大切な国民の命を 懸ける必要があるのかね 私は反対だよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 地下に閉じ込められた人間___不法労働者だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this categorizing judgment.

feedback.correct_en: This is an 'A は B だ' categorization: 'the people trapped underground = illegal laborers.' は identifies the topic being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn it into exhaustive listing ('it is the trapped people who are the laborers'), which doesn't match PM Amanuma's dismissive classification.

contrast_examples.en: He is the doctor (identification among others).

prompt.context_jp: 軋みと火花が暗がりに走る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 軋みと火花___暗がりに走る。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this cinematic new event.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator paints a sudden sensory event: creaking and sparks appear in the dark. が introduces these as newly perceived subjects.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would thematize creaks and sparks as if they were already under discussion — unnatural for a one-shot descriptive moment.

prompt.context_jp: 開いた口の奥は、光の届かぬ闇であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 開いた口の奥___、光の届かぬ闇であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this descriptive A は B copula sentence.

feedback.correct_en: A は B だ pattern describes a property of the topic (the opened mouth's depths = darkness). は establishes the topic for the characterization.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as exhaustive 'it is the depths that were darkness,' which is awkward for a scene-painting description.

contrast_examples.en: The back is (the dark part / specifically dark).

prompt.context_jp: 痙攣を起こしかけた患者の前で、弦巻の指先はわずかに震えていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 痙攣を起こしかけた患者の前___、弦巻の指先はわずかに震えていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the location of the action.

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action/event occurs — her fingertips tremble in front of the patient.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a static location of existence, not the setting of an action. を is the direct-object marker and doesn't fit a locative noun.

prompt.context_jp: 「人の命と命令 どっちが大事？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 人の命と命令、どっち___大事？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for a 'which of the two' question.

feedback.correct_en: どっち in an either/or comparison takes が — it demands an exhaustive, identifying answer ('which one, out of these two, is more important?').
feedback.incorrect_en: どっちは is ungrammatical in this comparison frame; the question requires picking out one, which is the job of exhaustive-listing が.

prompt.context_jp: 白金の足が止まり、赤塚もまた歩みを止めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 白金の足___止まり、赤塚もまた歩みを止めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this subordinate-clause subject.

feedback.correct_en: Subjects in subordinate ~て/連用 clauses typically take が, not は. Here 'Shirogane's feet stopped, and…' uses が to confine the subject to the first clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would try to make 白金の足 the topic of the whole sentence, but the next clause has a different subject (赤塚), so は would misread the structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降って、道が濡れた。
contrast_examples.en: It rained and the road got wet.
As for rain, it didn't fall.

prompt.context_jp: 背後にどんな影があったのかを知る者は、この国にほとんどいない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 背後にどんな影があったのかを知る者___、この国にほとんどいない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this long topic phrase.

feedback.correct_en: With negative/scarcity predicates like ほとんどいない, the topic normally takes は: 'as for those who know…, there are hardly any.' It frames and then contrasts with the ignorant majority.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as new-information subject, but the whole clause is a generic topic being commented on with a scope-negation — a classic は context.

contrast_examples.jp: それを知る人はほとんどいない。

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見は担架の柄を握り直し、頭を下げるほかなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見は担架の柄を握り直し、頭を下げる___なかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression meaning 'had no choice but to…'.

feedback.correct_en: 〜ほかない means 'there is no option other than…' — Kitami was blocked by the officer and had no choice but to bow his head.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜ことがない means 'has never done,' and 〜ものがない doesn't form the 'no choice but' pattern. Only ほか carries 'other than.'

contrast_examples.en: I had no choice but to give up.

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見は間髪を入れず担架をテントへと押し進めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見は___を入れず担架をテントへと押し進めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes the idiom meaning 'without a moment's delay.'

feedback.correct_en: 間髪を入れず is a fixed idiom literally 'without inserting a hair's breadth,' meaning 'instantly/without a moment's pause.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 間隔を入れず and 時間を入れず are not idiomatic — they'd just sound like awkward literal attempts to say 'without an interval.'

contrast_examples.jp: 少し間を置いて答えた。

prompt.context_jp: 「神経ガスの材料調達に 加担していた可能性が高い」
prompt.prompt_jp: 神経ガスの材料調達に加担していた___が高い。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun for 'the likelihood is high.'

feedback.correct_en: 可能性が高い is the stock collocation for 'the probability is high' used in investigative/analytical speech. Tsukishima is reporting likelihood.
feedback.incorrect_en: 確信 is personal certainty, not external probability. 気持ちが高い is not a natural collocation.

contrast_examples.jp: 犯人である可能性が高い。
contrast_examples.en: There's a high chance he's the culprit.

contrast_examples.jp: 犯人だと確信している。

prompt.context_jp: 「必ず見捨てる」
prompt.prompt_jp: 政府は必ず___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'abandon/forsake.'

feedback.correct_en: 見捨てる = to abandon/forsake someone in need. Tsukishima is saying the government will definitely cast these people aside.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見つける is 'to find,' 見送る is 'to see off' — neither captures the moral weight of 'abandon' Tsukishima is using to shock Otowa.

contrast_examples.en: See a friend off at the station.

prompt.context_jp: 「あなたとは 一生 腹を割って話すことはなさそうね」
prompt.prompt_jp: あなたとは一生___を割って話すことはなさそうね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the body part that completes the idiom 'speak frankly.'

feedback.correct_en: 腹を割って話す is the set idiom meaning 'speak with one's guts open' — i.e., openly and candidly. Shirogane doubts she'll ever reach that level with Akatsuka.
feedback.incorrect_en: 胸を割る isn't idiomatic; 心を開く exists but takes 開く, not 割る. The idiom pairs 腹 with 割る specifically.

contrast_examples.en: Let's open our hearts and talk.

prompt.context_jp: 「とにかく このことは 他言無用でお願いしますよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: とにかくこのことは___でお願いしますよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the compact formal expression meaning 'don't tell anyone.'

feedback.correct_en: 他言無用 is a four-character idiom literally 'other-words unnecessary,' meaning 'keep this to yourself.' Perfect for an NDA warning.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言語道断 means 'outrageous/unspeakable.' 問答無用 means 'no questions allowed/no debate.' Both are compact phrases but have completely different meanings.

contrast_examples.jp: このことは他言無用で。

prompt.context_jp: 「魚の目に水見えず 人の目に空見えず」
prompt.prompt_jp: 魚の目に水___ 、人の目に空___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the correct form for this proverb 'fish don't see water, people don't see sky.'

feedback.correct_en: The classical negative 〜ず preserves the proverb's archaic, aphoristic tone. The literary 見えず fits the formal, saying-like register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見えない is modern colloquial and breaks the parallel proverb rhythm. 見られず is passive/potential, which shifts the meaning away from 'invisible to them.'

prompt.context_jp: カルナのような日本語学習中の外国人労働者がたどたどしく話す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line best captures a non-native speaker struggling but earnest, as in the show?

choices.text: 僕たち 希望 持って 日本 来ました。みんな 真面目に働いてる。
私たちは希望を持って日本に参りまして、皆真面目に勤労しております。
俺ら希望あって日本来たっつーの、みんなちゃんと働いてんだっつの。

feedback.correct_en: The original drops particles (を, に) and keeps verbs short — a realistic portrayal of a learner speaking emotionally but with limited grammar. This matches Karna's actual lines.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses polished keigo (参りまして, 勤労) that no struggling learner would produce. C is rough native male slang that doesn't fit a worried foreign worker begging for help.

contrast_examples.jp: 私は日本が好きでございます。
contrast_examples.en: I am very fond of Japan (over-formal).

prompt.context_jp: 月島が音羽を突き放す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Tsukishima's cold brush-off?

choices.text: 好きにしろ。ただし我々は協力しない。
どうぞご自由になさってください。ただ、こちらは協力しかねます。
好きにしていいよ〜でも手伝わないからね。

feedback.correct_en: A is blunt command-form (〜しろ) with a flat ただし — exactly the dismissive, superior tone Tsukishima uses on Otowa.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly polite keigo that would signal respect, which contradicts his contempt. C's casual, friendly tone (〜してね) is far too soft for the hostile power dynamic.

prompt.context_jp: 駒場が千住に時間短縮を命じる場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line best matches Komaba's clipped command style?

choices.text: 8分でやっていただけますか。

feedback.correct_en: A is the plain imperative 〜ろ — fast, authoritative, and typical of a crisis-command register. Matches the actual line.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is deferential request language unfit for commanding subordinates in a crisis. C sounds unsure and casual — the opposite of Komaba's decisive tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 急いでいただけますか。

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見のMER理念を一文で表す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally expresses MER's creed?

choices.text: どんな命も救う。それがMERの存在意義です。
どんな命でも救う。それがMERの存在する理由です。
あらゆる命を救助する。それこそMERの存在性でございます。

feedback.correct_en: A uses the strongest emphatic quantifier 〜も with a concise 存在意義 — a crisp, moving creed line perfect for a drama climax.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 〜でも救う weakens to 'even,' and 存在する理由 is wordier and less punchy. C's 救助する + 存在性 is stiff bureaucratic Japanese that would deflate the emotional moment.

contrast_examples.en: We save even anyone (weaker, more conditional).

prompt.context_jp: 赤塚が官邸を立ち去る時の皮肉を込めた一言。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best captures Akatsuka's politely barbed exit line?

choices.text: では失礼します。総理官邸は今の私の居場所ではないので。
じゃ、帰るわ。ここ、俺の場所じゃないし。
これにて御無礼仕ります。首相官邸は今、私の居場所に非ざれば。

feedback.correct_en: A keeps standard polite 〜ます with a half-finished 〜ので, which lets the implied barb ('…so I'll be going') land coolly. This matches the aired line.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too casual for a governor addressing cabinet-level figures. C is archaic/samurai register that would sound bizarre in a modern political setting.

contrast_examples.jp: 場違いなので失礼します。
contrast_examples.en: I don't belong here, so excuse me (polite jab).
I'm out of place, so I'm leaving (blunt).
